title: VP of Public Policy, Major Cloud & AI Platforms
summary: Public policy leaders representing major cloud and frontier AI platforms advocate for a targeted, two-track regulatory system. They accept federal oversight and mandatory safety evaluations for frontier models—conceptually modeled after FINRA-style self-regulatory organizations—in exchange for federal preemption of state-level laws and statutory safe harbors against strict developer liability.
red_lines: A 50-state patchwork of un-preempted state AI legislation.
Imposition of strict, unbounded developer liability for downstream third-party model misuse or jailbreaks.
Input-based regulation that micromanages model architecture or training data collection (defending fair use for web scraping).
tradeoffs: Offering advanced frontier models to government AI Safety Institutes for pre-deployment testing in exchange for federal preemption of state regulations.
Accepting mandatory incident reporting and transparency measures (such as watermarking) in exchange for statutory safe harbor protections against liability.
engagement: Bifurcated: collaborative, pragmatic, and ethical-framework driven in multilateral forums (OECD, UN, Congress) to narrow the scope of harm; aggressively transactional at state and electoral levels, deploying Super PACs, lobbying, and competitiveness arguments against restrictive laws.
